summary: The anchors show the design is currently encoded mostly as duplicated prose and shell snippets, with only template/parity tests enforcing parts of the contract. The largest risks are execution semantics, concurrent staging, evidence verification, auditability, and the ambiguity of per-file blueprints.

suggestions.title: Extract §3b into one checked helper
suggestions.rationale: The commands prescribe staging, rendering, subprocess execution, validation, and triage manually, but no executable helper guarantees that every failure becomes a recorded skip while `/sdd-spec` continues. A shared helper invoked by both command surfaces would make those semantics testable and prevent twin behavior from diverging.

suggestions.title: Make research staging run-scoped and collision-safe
suggestions.rationale: The deterministic `sdd/state/.design_research/<feature-name>` directory is created with `mkdir -p`, so concurrent runs or an interrupted rerun can mix briefs, logs, and suggestions. Use a unique staging directory plus an atomic final move that fails if the destination already exists, and test concurrent/rerun behavior.

suggestions.title: Resolve the foreground-versus-background contract
suggestions.rationale: The design rules and repository policy describe a background reviewer, while the current §3b instructions explicitly run Codex synchronously for up to 600 seconds. Since `sdd-planner` waits for `/sdd-spec` and treats command failure as fatal, this can stall unattended planning even though the phase is called non-blocking; the implementation needs one explicit lifecycle and a test for timeout behavior.

suggestions.title: Reject paths outside the repository root
suggestions.rationale: The schema accepts arbitrary strings and the triage instructions only use `test -e`, so absolute paths, `../` traversal, or symlink escapes can pass the stated verification. Canonicalize every affected path against the repository root, reject escapes and non-regular files, and add cases for absolute, traversal, and symlink paths.

suggestions.title: Require line or symbol evidence, not paths alone
suggestions.rationale: The output contract records only `affected_paths`, while the command can verify existence without proving which code claim was checked. This is weaker than the repository’s existing review policy and its `verified: path:line` convention; add structured evidence containing path plus line, symbol, or quoted claim, and require triage to record the verification result.

suggestions.title: Persist a replayable Codex execution record
suggestions.rationale: The proposed `-o` file is only the structured result, and the command redirects ordinary stdout/stderr to `codex.log` without requesting the dispatcher’s JSON event stream. That does not reliably capture the exact invocation, CLI version, model, timeout, exit status, and raw response needed to audit or reproduce a decision; persist those fields alongside the brief and result.

suggestions.title: Validate triage completeness mechanically
suggestions.rationale: The suggestion schema allows duplicate IDs, empty strings, and empty `affected_paths`, while the §9 rows, disposition counts, and `Landed in` values are written manually. Add a triage schema/validator that requires exactly one disposition and reason per suggestion, rejects unknown or duplicate IDs, and derives the summary counts; test missing, duplicated, and extra rows.

suggestions.title: Use patch-shaped blueprints for file edits
suggestions.rationale: A MODIFY blueprint currently says to insert below a quoted anchor, but does not specify occurrence count, replacement/deletion semantics, or enough context to disambiguate repeated anchors. This can duplicate imports or registrations; emit a validated patch or explicit edit operation with unique context and run an apply-check before handing it to the executor.

suggestions.title: Enforce blueprint completeness against the file table
suggestions.rationale: The current tests assert that the template contains blueprint headings, but no check validates generated task files against their declared files or the blueprint quality rules in `/sdd-task`. Add validation for one block per declared file, matching CREATE/MODIFY action, bounded `FILL IN` markers, populated Why text, valid contract anchors, and the stated size cap.

suggestions.title: Frame the recommended option as a hypothesis to challenge
suggestions.rationale: The neutral brief includes the accepted “Recommended Option” directly, even though the review policy forbids feeding a preferred conclusion. This creates anchoring toward confirmation; retain the accepted scope for context but label the recommendation as a hypothesis and require the reviewer to test its assumptions or name a viable alternative.

suggestions.title: Validate the probe’s actual result and configuration
suggestions.rationale: The probe records success solely from Codex’s exit code; it does not verify that the output contains exactly `OK`, that the requested model was used, or that the requested reasoning setting was accepted. A false-positive probe can still lead to a 600-second research call and an inaccurately completed status; validate the output and retain the probe metadata.
